regime_context: Hong Kong shows a narrow, non-directional rotation: only 4 of 17 themes are trend-eligible, led by Banks and Energy with weak separation (0.168 margin). The headline Banks theme is crowded (z=1.02) and mean-reverting, while the most macro-visible theme (AI/Tech) sits deep in the ineligible bottom ranks. This is a defensive/income-favored tape where almost every theme is unscorable — most calls can only be directional expressions, not proxy-gradeable.
emerging_watch: Watch whether Energy (H-shares) can widen its margin over Banks (H + HK) beyond 0.4 in score. I would retire this watch if Banks re-assert a score lead of 0.3 or more, or if Energy's Hurst tag decays from 'trend' to 'mixed' before the end of the month.

theses.subject: Banks (H + HK)
theses.thesis: Banks are the confirmed leader (rank 1, eligible, strong breadth 0.769) and the only theme combining leadership with trend eligibility. Its mean-revert Hurst tag and crowded flag (z=1.02) argue the easy trend is over and any entry is late, so this is a caution-capped carry lean, not a chase; the trend gate is still open (eligible=true), which is the detector's only validated edge and keeps it in the stay-long camp rather than forcing de-risk.
theses.dissent: A crowded, mean-reverting leader with unscheduled macro surprise share at 1.0 is exactly the setup where reflexivity unwinds fast; its 25% headline weight means index-level shocks hit hardest right here.

theses.thesis: This is the only scorable theme on the board (proxy 3033.HK) and it sits at rank 13, ineligible, with negative score, weak breadth (0.444), and a 0.34 durability bar.
